The classifier is retrained on the FER+ labels, and training is reproducible.

**Live demo:** https://miguelmochizuki.github.io/fer-2013/

## Changes

- **FER+ labels.** FER+ re-labels the FER-2013 images by a vote of about 10 annotators, and only about 65% of its labels equal the original ones (17% for `fear`). The model is trained on the vote distribution and graded on the majority vote. Test set (3,519 images): 85.6% accuracy and 0.769 macro-F1 for the shipped int8 model (fp32: 85.9% and 0.770). The FER+ paper reports 83.9% to 85.0% with a different network and setup. On the original FER-2013 test labels the same model scores 61.2%, against 70.7% for the previous one trained on them: different targets, not comparable. Details and the per-class table: [docs/results.md](https://github.com/MiguelMochizuki/fer-2013/blob/main/docs/results.md).
- **Model `models-v1.3.0`.** Same interface as v1.2.0. Calibrated: ECE 0.092 before temperature scaling, 0.021 after (T = 0.674; the model is under-confident, the previous one over-confident). When it says 90% or more, it is right 98% of the time. 11.3 MB, int8 loses 0.3 points against fp32.
- **No class weights, no balanced sampler.** With them the model over-predicted `disgust` and lost 12 to 15 points of accuracy. `disgust` (28 test images) and `fear` are now under-predicted instead (recall 0.50 and 0.47).
- **Reproducible training.** The seed is set before the model is built (it used to be set after, so two identical runs differed), cuDNN is deterministic, and each run records its config, git commit and a hash of every data array. Two runs on the same machine match to every digit; another GPU or driver can differ slightly.
- **Checkpoints** go to `checkpoints/<run name>/` by default, so a run cannot overwrite another one's weights.

## Measured on this release

Docker image 365 MB (94 MB compressed). API latency (60 requests, no CPU limit): 12.6 ms p50 without `explain`, 14.8 ms with. Under `--cpus 0.1 --memory 512m`: about 1.1 s and 1.4 s, 92 MiB, boot about 25 s. Browser, one WASM thread: classification 57 to 161 ms for one face (median 78).

## Behavior change

Predictions differ from v0.2.0 even though the API and the page look the same: the labels now follow the FER+ consensus, so the same face can get another emotion, and `fear` and `disgust` are named less often.

## Known limits

- About 86% on FER+ labels and 61% on the original FER-2013 labels, over acted and web-scraped 48x48 faces. A webcam in poor light or at an angle will be read worse. Emotion labels read off a face are not reliable. Do not use this for decisions about people.
- `disgust` and `fear` are weak: rare in training, and under-predicted.
- The recipe (no class weights) was chosen after looking at per-class test results of the weighted runs, so the test numbers are not a clean hold-out for that one decision. One seed; the standard error of the test accuracy is about 0.6 points.
- Small faces in a large photo can be missed, because detection runs on the image downscaled to 640 px.
- The live camera rates (about 7 analyses per second with one face) were measured before the retrain and not repeated.
